name.en: Fake income tax refund: “refund approved, verify your account”

how.en: After the return-filing season, an SMS or email in the Income Tax Department's name says a refund has been approved, or that refunds above a limit need “manual verification”. It asks you to confirm or update your bank account through a link. The page copies the e-filing portal and steals your PAN, bank details, card numbers and passwords. The department does not ask for bank details or send refund links by SMS or email.

text.en: A message in the Income Tax Department's name says a refund is approved or pending.
It asks you to verify or update your bank account by link.
It warns the refund will be cancelled if you don't act soon.
The page asks for net banking login, card details or OTP.
ITD: As per your ITR, a refund of Rs 18,250 is approved and will be credited to your account ending xx41. If this account is wrong, update your bank details here: [link]
Subject: Income tax refund on hold. Your refund needs manual verification before release. Complete verification within 48 hours using the link below or the refund will lapse.

en: income tax refund sms with link
refund approved verify via link income tax
income tax manual verification email for refund
itr refund message asked for bank details
fake income tax department refund email
tax refund will lapse verify now
A refund message with a link.
A refund that will lapse unless you act.
Check refund status only by logging in to the official e-filing portal yourself.
If you entered bank details, call your bank and 1930.
